brief: Explain the fall in review strength before any guardrail relies on it (Lean flow study, owner ruling R13). Real-catch blocked verdicts per reviewed pull request fell from 0.52 over round 10's first six days (112 pull requests) to 0.15 in the 48 h before the flow plan's adoption (47 pull requests), before any flow change merged; bookkeeping blocks held near 0.6 per pull request. Measure, on the review and verdict bus refs and the merged pull requests, which of these moves the rate: the mix of pull requests reviewed (product against instrument and process, size), the reviewer seat's model and agent kind (nudge.md replaced dead Opus seats with other models), fixer quality (first-pass merge share by fixer model), the verdict carries that replace re-reviews, and the real-catch classes themselves. Each candidate is a stratified rate with its own count, and a null control stratum whose rate must not move. Deliver the explanation and a recommended threshold for the review-strength guardrail; until it lands the guardrail reports the rate and trips on nothing. Follow D13's required outputs where they apply.
